records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readInteger() accepts non-minimal INTEGER encodings (leading 0x00 padding in R/S) which are then silently normalized by integerToBytes(), enabling signature malleability
records.rationale: In the new ECDSA conversion logic, `ASN1Decoder.readInteger()` (new file) parses the INTEGER value as `new BigInteger(bytes)` without enforcing DER minimal encoding rules (e.g., rejecting unnecessary leading 0x00). In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().asn1derToConcatenatedRS`, the parsed `BigInteger` is then converted back to fixed-size bytes via `integerToBytes`, which truncates/pads to `len`. This combination will normalize different DER encodings of the same integer value (including non-minimal encodings) into the same fixed-length R/S, which is the malleability mechanism

records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider (typically Sun JCE) instead of BouncyCastle, returning a wrong-but-plausible value
records.rationale: In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()`, the method returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, i.e., the provider backing the *default keystore type* (typically the JDK's `SUN` provider for `JKS`), not a BouncyCastle provider. Given the method contract/name in `CryptoProvider` (`getBouncyCastleProvider()`), this is a wrong-but-plausible value that can cause callers expecting BC to get a different provider.

records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readSequence silently accepts indefinite-length BER encoding as empty/truncated sequence because readLength() returns -1 which the while (length > 0) loop treats as done, producing no clear error
records.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readLength(), an initial length byte of 0x80 returns -1 to represent indefinite-length encoding (`if (length == 0x80) { return -1; }`). In ASN1Decoder.readSequence(), the returned value is used as the loop bound (`int length = readLength(); ... while (length > 0) { ... }`). If an indefinite-length SEQUENCE is encountered, `length` becomes -1 and the loop is skipped, returning an empty `List<byte[]>` without raising an error, effectively silently accepting/truncating the sequence.
